heat haze was an abundance, and she almost was close to tossing off her red cloak. but someone might have seen who she was then, and she had also been quite careful to conceal her face with a dusty scarf. the village had been abuzz all week over the red comet, some men had searched the area and found nothing but a blackened crater. empty, and one that had formed with no blast or noise. her intuition was twitching though, to further explore the area, for something must have come.

she snapped to attention as she crept along, when the normal bird cries were interrupted by a monotone sing-song. she looked for the source, what animal could have made the noise and saw, just bushes and leaves. a slight shimmer behind the trees? no, she said to herself as she looked closer, it was only a heat mirage curling through thin dew-dissolved mist.

she tentatively carried forward, wary for any adults that might be here too. she was still grounded for sneaking into the late night feast. she saw none, and after some hand-wringing decision hurried on her way to the crater. it was easy enough to find, for it broadcast a thick trail of smoke up from the valley it had landed in. the valley it sat in didnt even realize there was a problem, and the water still ran clear, sunshine still blazed white and the birds still sang.

and, the crater was far bigger and deeper then the adults had implied. a horse and rider could have stood in it with no problem. she said aloud "so big", in a whisper to herself. an easygoing voice behind her, strangely accented and speaking of kids who set fire to animals behind the cow sheds, said "quite small actually. i tried to be economical in getting here, and that meant coalescing and free falling". the very air strained suddenly with fear, and she didn't turn around. the voice said "how would you like to hear an offer? if its any consolation your perfect, for it"

I'm a bit worried that Voat will meet the same fate as reddit.

Then again, reddit was part of a corporation and voat isn't (as far as I know)

Maddox refused to advertise despite being one of the most popular original websites, so there's that. Perhaps there is hope for the sites run by individuals.
Is corruption inevitable when a site gets huge?

Corruption will always sprout up. The degree to which corruption manifests itself and where it pops up is what's important, and that depends on a number of factors...Atko seems to be doing solidly and is polling Voat every step of the way, so I'm not worrying.

reddit didn't start corporate owned, it became that way some time after. Could you really blame Atko if some suit showed up and offered him a very large amount of money for the site, and he sold? What if the amount of money guaranteed him and his family comfort for the rest of their lives, could he really pass that up?

No. Corruption is possible at all levels- big or small. The only difference between a big site and a small site is the amount of resources corrupting agents will devote to the critical nodes in large networks versus critical nodes in small networks. However, as long as moral hazard remains both in effect and a major barrier to entry for corrupting agents, then corruption can be minimized at all levels. Moral hazard is a set of rules and standard operating procedures to respond to power users who violate a sites rules- automatically and strictly. In other words, as long as mods face a realistic threat of being banned and their subs closed or locked down, then corruption can be controlled.

Am I naive to say that it depends on the people involved? If nine people have strong morals and one person does not, then corruption should not exist because the majority would kick out the minority. The inverse is also true. Does this then mean that the faults begin when hiring people with some power within the company?
